simple.meaning: מַכְבָּר (makbâr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a cloth (as netted).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 1 time across 2 Kings, beginning at 2 Kings 8:15. Its contexts include death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַכְבָּר (H4346).

definitions.full: H4346. mikbar מִכְבָּר noun masculine grating or lattice-work , construct מִכְבַּר ; — Exod 27:4 and thou shalt make for it (the altar of burnt-offering in the tabernacle) נְהשֶׁת רֶשֶׁת מַעֲשֵׂה מִכְבָּר a grating , (even) a network of bronze, which surrounded the lower half of the altar ( 27:5 b): so 38:4 ; הַנְּחשֶׁת מִכְבַּר 35:16 ; 38:5 , 30 ; 39:39 .
definitions.rootNote: from 3527 in the sense of covering; (compare 4345 )

occurrences.englishText: On the next day, he took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died. Then Hazael reigned in his place.
